absent: Values, defaults and parameter wiring of run_test_mask, sequential_test_order, test_repeat_count, test_loop_count, nr_threads, nr_pages and nr_pcpu_objects.
Definitions and lifecycle of prepare_for_test_srcu, test_n_undone, test_all_done_comp, test_report_one_done, start_comp and all_done_comp.
Bodies of the alloc tests named in the case table but outside these fragments and of no_block_alloc_test and align_shift_alloc_test expected failure reasons.
Remainder of check_xa_shrink beyond the shown prefix and bodies of check_insert, check_cmpxchg and check_cmpxchg_order.
Workqueue creation flag effects, queued work scheduling behavior and sysfs affinity scope semantics.
Numeric values of page size, page shift, NUMA node sentinel, allocation flags, XArray marks and retry sentinels.

findings.text: Small test record combining a deferred reclamation callback header with a twenty byte scratch area used to hold a marker before deferred release.

Test descriptor carrying a display name, a no argument test routine returning integer status, and a flag marking expected failure; the global table instantiates thirteen named cases in fixed order with two flagged as expected to fail.
Per case accounting with separate tallies for passed, failed and expected failed runs plus an averaged duration in microseconds.

Per worker state holding a thread handle, a per case accounting array sized by the case table, and start and stop cycle stamps; a global pointer references a worker count sized allocation of such records.
Benchmark thread context holding a completion for work signalling, an embeddable work item, a pointer to a latency array, an assigned processor number and a per thread item count.

Percpu stress allocates a pointer vector for a configured object count, then for each slot chooses a small random size and a power of two alignment bounded by page shift, attempts allocation and records failure but continues, finally releases every slot and the vector and reports aggregate status; when per cpu kind memory is required the body is omitted and success is reported.

Two loops each repeat a configured number of times allocating one page, writing a marker to the start of the scratch area, then handing the block to deferred release, one through a sleepable single argument path and the other through a two argument path naming the embedded callback header; allocation failure aborts with an error.

Page mapping check ensures at least one page, allocates a page pointer vector, bulk allocates that many pages, then repeatedly maps them contiguously, writes a marker to the mapping start and unmaps; all acquired pages and the vector are released and the result signals whether the acquired count matched the request.

Reallocation check iterates a configured loop count, each pass starting from an empty handle to obtain one page and verifying a marker survives a grow to four pages, a shrink crossing a page boundary, a shrink inside one page, and a grow inside the retained page, freeing the final block each pass and aborting on any allocation or content mismatch.
In place permutation walks indices downward swapping each position with a randomly chosen lower position bounded by the current index.

Worker routine builds an identity ordering of case indices, optionally permutes it, waits on a startup barrier, stamps a start cycle count, then for each mask enabled case times repeated executions tallying passed versus expected failed versus failed, stores an averaged microsecond duration, stamps a stop count, announces completion once, and idles with short sleeps until asked to stop.
Result classification treats zero status as passed, nonzero status on a case flagged expected fail as expected failed, and other nonzero status as failed.

Startup normalization clamps the requested worker count into a positive range with a large upper bound, allocates the worker state vector, and coerces nonpositive repeat and loop counts to one, reporting allocation failure.

Concurrent harness configures workers, holds a sleepable read side gate while launching one named thread per worker and counting successful starts, releases the gate to begin, blocks on a global completion with a periodic timeout, then stops each started thread, logs per enabled case tallies with repeat and loop settings and averaged durations plus per worker cycle elapsed, and releases the worker vector.
Module initialization entry executes the concurrent harness immediately and remains loaded only for a builtin build, otherwise returning a code that unloads the module.
Workqueue benchmark identity uses queue name bench_wq and expanded sysfs path /sys/bus/workqueue/devices/bench_wq/affinity_scope; default per thread item count is fifty thousand.
Benchmark iterates affinity scopes in order cpu, smt, cache_shard, cache, numa and system, using each label both as the value written to sysfs and as the report tag.

Work handler recovers its enclosing thread context and signals its completion; the thread routine waits for a global start signal, then per item resets its completion, initializes its work item, timestamps queue submission, stores the elapsed nanoseconds, waits for the handler, and when the last thread finishes signals global completion before idling until stop.
Comparator for 64 bit unsigned values returns negative, positive or zero according to strict ordering or equality.
Scope setter opens the workqueue affinity path write only, writes the supplied scope text from the start, closes the handle and propagates open or write failures.

Single scope run applies the scope, allocates thread contexts, thread handles and a merged latency buffer plus per thread latency buffers with staged cleanup on failure, resets shared counters and start and done signals, creates and binds one thread per online processor up to the requested count with early release of the start gate on creation failure, times the collective run, flushes the queue, joins all threads, merges and sorts all latencies and reports throughput with fiftieth ninetieth and ninety fifth percentile latencies before freeing all allocations.

Benchmark init validates a positive item count, creates an unbound sysfs workqueue with no reserved threads, runs the scoped benchmark for a thread count bounded by online processors, destroys the queue and returns a code that unloads the module after reporting.
Xarray test tallies count total assertions and passed assertions as unsigned integers; the multi index order bound equals the machine word width when multi support is enabled and one otherwise.
Dump helper is an empty operation; assertion helper always counts a run, counts a pass when its predicate is false, otherwise logs the caller and line and dumps the array and stack.

Small helpers encode an index as a value with the sign bit cleared, then wrap store, insert, allocate and erase operations asserting expected return identity, allocated identifier equality and post erase absence.

Ordered store builds an ordered cursor and under exclusive access retries the store while reporting allocation shortage for the requested allocation mode; the public mark setter serializes an internal mark update with array lock acquisition and release.
Public array operation setting a caller supplied mark at a caller supplied index within a caller supplied array.

Error and retry checks assert success of basic store and erase, kernel mode store after nowait attempts, value overwrite semantics, find and reload behavior across erase with retry signalling and iterator recovery, and replacement of retry placeholders by iteration stores.

Load, mark and iteration checks verify incremental population and removal over a thousand indices, absence of marks on empty slots, mark set and query isolation between marks, clearing of marks on erase, union of marks when a larger ordered entry covers marked slots with exactly two visible entries and one marked entry, plus bulk marking over a thousand indices with marked iteration count and per entry mark initialization.

Shrink check starts from an empty array with two adjacent entries, then under exclusive access verifies loaded values and locked slot contents, removes one entry and asserts the cursor reports bounds, the vacated node slot shows a retry marker and subsequent loads observe absence.

Vmalloc tests gate worker start with a sleepable barrier and announce completion through a global completion; workqueue bench coordinates start and finish with global completions plus per thread completions and a shared done counter; xarray checks bracket lock free traversal with read side sections and serialize mutation and cursor use with array and cursor locks.

Allocation and thread creation failures propagate as negative status with staged release of already acquired vectors, pages, latency buffers and threads; scope file open or write errors abort a benchmark run; timed waits use a periodic timeout to avoid hung task reports.
